news.title: Netflix secures exclusive 2030 World Cup broadcast rights in Spain
news.lede: Netflix added to its sports portfolio on Tuesday by landing the rights to broadcast the 2030 World Cup to the viewing audience in Spain and Andorra. Spain is one of three main co-hosts of the next edition of the FIFA World Cup, along with Portugal and Morocco. The first three games of the tournament will take place in South America. While FIFA prefers a free over-the-air broadcast partner over a streaming service, the deal includes a plan to air one match per day on public television.

news.title: New Zealand lose 4-0 to impressive Morocco at FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup
news.lede: New Zealand have lost their opening game at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup, beaten 4-0 by hosts Morocco. The Young Football Ferns put up strong resistance in a scoreless first half, with goalkeeper Nienke Holland thwarting the wave of Moroccan attacks that created 16 attempts on goal. Led by Holland’s example, the New Zealand defenders scrambled to keep an impressive Morocco side at bay. Main photo: The New Zealanders block a Moroccan attack.

news.title: Messi's Argentina to face Spain in 2026 World Cup final at MetLife Stadium
news.lede: Argentina will meet Spain in the 2026 FIFA World Cup final on Sunday, July 19, at 3 p.m. at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey. Lionel Messi could win his second World Cup title as the defending champions take on a Spain team that has conceded just one goal in the entire tournament. Spain reached the final by beating France, a two-time World Cup winner, 2-0 on Tuesday. France had been considered a strong contender after topping the FIFA men's ranking.

news.title: All 47 Saudi Pro League players selected for 2026 FIFA World Cup
news.lede: The 2026 FIFA World Cup will feature some of the biggest names in world football, and the Saudi Pro League is set to have a sizeable presence on the sport’s biggest stage. A total of 47 players from 18 national teams, including 25 representing Saudi Arabia, are contracted to Saudi Pro League clubs heading into the tournament, underlining the league’s growing influence beyond the Kingdom. That figure rises to 49 players from 19 nations when including Curaçao defender Juriën Gaari of Abha and Saudi Arabia goalkeeper Mohammed Al-Owais of Al-Ula, who both play outside the Saudi top flight.
